Flooding Disrupts Chemical Production and Supply Chains in Sri Lanka

Severe flooding in southwestern Sri Lanka is causing major disruptions across the country’s chemicals industry, with several production facilities and key transport routes affected as heavy rains continue for a fifth consecutive day. The ongoing deluge, which the Sri Lanka Meteorological Department describes as the heaviest in the region since 2017, has inundated industrial zones in Kalutara and Galle, areas home to many of the nation’s chemical processing plants.

Many manufacturers, including GulfChem Lanka and Suriya Industrial Chemicals, have ceased operations amid rising floodwaters, while logistics firms report significant delays in the movement of raw materials and finished goods. “Road access to our Kalutara site is completely cut off. We have halted all production since Tuesday morning,” said Nuwan Perera, operations manager at GulfChem Lanka. “We are currently assessing the extent of the damage to our equipment and stored chemicals.”

The floods have also interrupted supply routes from the main port of Colombo to inland distribution hubs, compounding concerns over inventory shortages. According to the Sri Lanka Chemical Manufacturers’ Association (SLCMA), at least seven major production facilities are offline, with another five operating at reduced capacity due to difficulties sourcing inputs or transporting products. “Our members are facing unprecedented logistical challenges,” said SLCMA Chairperson Dinali Jayasuriya. “Many chemicals are time-sensitive, and prolonged storage during these conditions increases the risk of spoilage or hazardous incidents.”

Analysts estimate that the industry could see output losses of up to 40 percent this week if the situation persists. The Ceylon Chemical Workers Union has voiced concern for more than 2,000 employees in affected zones, noting that evacuation orders and transport shutdowns are limiting staff availability. “Worker safety is our primary concern, but the economic impact for employees and their families will be significant,” said union president Mahesh Fernando.

The Meteorological Department forecasts continued heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours, with authorities urging chemical facilities to implement emergency safety protocols and monitor local conditions closely.
